articleMarkdown:
# Studying Great Accumulation: turning stored strength into real capacity

When you have strength, first learn restraint and practice, so that accumulation becomes the ability to take things on.

Knowing many things and spending much time do not necessarily equip us for complex tasks. Great Accumulation joins storing up with restraint: being able to advance and stop, learn from predecessors, and undertake new action when conditions fit. It is not a slogan that more stockpiling is always better.

## Identifying the hexagram

Dà Xù is hexagram 26 in the traditional King Wen sequence, with the symbol ䷙. Its lower trigram is Qian ☰ and its upper trigram is Gen ☶; their traditional images are heaven and mountain, respectively. Count the lines from the bottom: 初九, 九二, 九三, 六四, 六五, 上九. A solid line is yang and a broken line is yin. Nine and six in the line headings identify yang and yin; they do not indicate additional lines.

The six lines are numbered from the bottom upward; the figure below displays their actual positions from top to bottom.

```text
━━━━━━  上九
━━  ━━  六五
━━  ━━  六四
━━━━━━  九三
━━━━━━  九二
━━━━━━  初九
```

## Hexagram statement

> 大畜：利貞，不家食吉，利涉大川。

Editorial rendering: Great Accumulation: right constancy is beneficial. Not eating at home brings good fortune; it is favorable to cross the great river.

Legge explicitly discusses both restraint and accumulation in xu, reading “not eating at home” within the ancient setting of entering public service and receiving support. Crossing the river remains an image of a major undertaking. This cannot be simplified to good luck from eating out.

A contemporary question is how knowledge and ability move beyond a private collection to serve real tasks. Going out requires preparation, while preparation needs a purpose it is meant to serve.

[zhouyi-26; legge1882-26]

## Interpretation in the Ten Wings

The Commentary on the Judgment (Tuan zhuan) and the Commentary on the Images (Xiang zhuan) belong to the Yi zhuan, the commentaries commonly called the Ten Wings. Their interpretations are kept separate below from the hexagram and line statements, followed by applications for contemporary learning.

The Commentary on the Judgment discusses the ability to restrain strength and renew virtue daily. The Commentary on the Images takes heaven within the mountain and emphasizes learning former words and deeds to cultivate virtue. Predecessors’ conduct and speech become learning material here.

When reading experiences and cases today, ask under which conditions they worked, then test understanding through practice. Collecting many materials is not understanding, and copying earlier choices is not the same as gaining judgment.

[zhouyi-26; hon-sep]

## Six lines, from bottom to top

The quotations below are line statements; the explanations that follow are original learning commentary. Good fortune, no blame, and regret belong to ancient divinatory language and cannot be turned directly into guarantees about an individual’s future.

### 初九 · Know when to stop first

> 有厲，利已。

Editorial rendering: There is danger. It is beneficial to stop.

Danger is present and stopping is beneficial: that is Legge’s explicit reading of the opening. Stopping can itself be a grounded action.

When offered a task beyond your preparation, clarify its conditions before accepting merely to look capable. Explain actual limits when delaying or declining, rather than letting anxiety decide everything.

[zhouyi-26; legge1882-26]

### 九二 · Do not force progress before conditions are ready

> 輿說輹。

Editorial rendering: The carriage’s axle-fastening comes loose.

A component of a carriage comes loose, preventing normal travel. Legge uses the image to explain restrained movement; the exact construction of an ancient carriage part should not be casually modernized.

While a crucial piece of information remains unconfirmed, complete other preparations. Knowing what is missing brings you closer to a solution than repeatedly urging yourself to hurry.

[zhouyi-26; legge1882-26]

### 九三 · Connect practice with the actual undertaking

> 良馬逐，利艱貞，吉。日閑輿衛，利有攸往。

Editorial rendering: Fine horses pursue their course. Difficulty joined with right constancy is beneficial; good fortune. Practice driving and protection daily; it is favorable to have somewhere to go.

Good horses, driving, and training in protection appear together. Legge stresses daily practice of the relevant abilities alongside awareness of the journey’s difficulties.

For example, when preparing to lead a discussion, rehearse the opening, time allocation, and responses to questions. Practice should resemble the real task, not merely repeat the most familiar and satisfying parts.

[zhouyi-26; legge1882-26]

### 六四 · Restraints can be established while a problem is still small

> 童牛之牿，元吉。

Editorial rendering: A wooden restraint at a young ox’s horns. Great good fortune.

In the chosen traditional reading, gu is a wooden fitting placed at a young ox’s horns. Legge uses it as an image of restraint established in advance. This belongs to an ancient animal-husbandry setting.

The contemporary analogy concerns only setting appropriate conditions early, such as agreeing clear rules and timely feedback steps. It supplies no animal-handling methods and does not use the management of livestock as a pretext to control people.

[zhouyi-26; legge1882-26]

### 六五 · Address causes, not only visible symptoms

> 豶豕之牙，吉。

Editorial rendering: The tusks of a castrated pig. Good fortune.

Fen shi is a castrated pig whose tusks remain; traditional interpretation uses it to show a change in the force behind danger. Legge develops his account of restraint through this image.

Contemporary learning can ask whether repeated problems have adjustable conditions behind them, instead of fighting the same surface effect each time. This analogy permits neither coercion nor harm to people, and does not turn ancient husbandry judgments into modern science.

[zhouyi-26; legge1882-26]

### 上九 · When space opens, put what you have accumulated to use

> 何天之衢，亨。

Editorial rendering: How broad heaven’s thoroughfare! Favorable progress.

Heaven’s thoroughfare brings a broad road into the final line. Legge reads it as the end of a period of restraint, with fuller room for strength to be exercised.

When sufficiently prepared, accept a real task of clear scope and expose your learning to feedback. Preparing forever without trying can also disconnect learning from actual needs.

[zhouyi-26; legge1882-26]

## From collected research to an actual presentation

Original contemporary scenario

The following contemporary scenario was created for learning.

A learner has collected extensive local-history materials but still cannot explain the changes on one street to someone else. She first chooses a small scope, checks sources, separates uncertain parts of the story, and asks someone familiar with the subject to hear a rehearsal.

The rehearsal reveals that the problem is not insufficient information but unclear sequence and terminology. She revises accordingly, confirms the venue, timing, and audience needs, and finally undertakes a short presentation.

Great Accumulation here involves restraint, accumulation, and use. Results come from understanding, practice, and real feedback, which the number of collected materials cannot replace.

## Common misreadings

1. Great Accumulation does not mean suppressing all action: a thoroughfare appears at the end. Preparation and practice should test each other.

2. The ancient images of ox, pig, and carriage supply no practical methods for safety, animal training, or controlling others. The hexagram also cannot predict investment holdings, health, or career success.

## Three practices

1. Choose one area of knowledge you are accumulating and identify the specific task it should help accomplish.

2. Find a small exercise close to the real task and check what still needs strengthening.

3. List separately the conditions necessary to begin and the preparation that need not be expanded further.

## Related reading

### Small Restraint (hexagram-09)

Small Restraint helps examine restraint and refinement within a limited scope; Great Accumulation develops fuller preparation and its use. Their smallness and greatness do not refer simply to money or scale: each line image and interpretation must be read separately.

## Closing question

When reading Great Accumulation, ask: how has what I have accumulated actually changed my ability to do things?

## Textual note

The fourth six uses the explicitly listed variant 牿, while the page’s main text has 告. The second nine retains that page’s 輹, and the third nine retains the 吉 present in that edition.
